item.title: The topics
item.description:
The processor creates no topic. The cluster’s owner creates the topics and their ACLs before it starts. The kind overlay does it with a Job that runs deploy/kind/kafka/topics.sh.

Logging in as the admin

Kafka’s tools read the admin’s login from a properties file. Over mTLS, it is a certificate and key in one PEM file, and the cluster’s CA:

security.protocol=SSL
ssl.keystore.type=PEM
ssl.keystore.location=/etc/kafka-admin/tls/tls.pem
ssl.truststore.type=PEM
ssl.truststore.location=/etc/kafka-admin/tls/ca.crt

kafka runs one of the tools with it:

item.title: The projection
item.description:
The projection keeps every event it applied, and each order’s status, folded from its events. The store package reads and writes it, and the projector package folds it.

The schema

store/schema.sql:

CREATE TABLE order_events (
 source_partition integer NOT NULL,
 source_offset bigint NOT NULL,
 order_id text NOT NULL,
 type text NOT NULL,
 at timestamptz NOT NULL,
 PRIMARY KEY (source_partition, source_offset)
);

CREATE INDEX order_events_by_order ON order_events (order_id, at);

CREATE TABLE order_status (
 order_id text PRIMARY KEY,
 status text NOT NULL,
 at timestamptz NOT NULL
);

An event is keyed by the partition and offset it was consumed from on orders.events, so a redelivery is found by them.

item.title: Projecting an event
item.description:
The projector

The projector package’s Projector is the queue.Processor of kafka.Messages that the Service runs. It takes the store and its Producers as interfaces, so its unit tests can give it their own:

type Store interface {
	Applied(ctx context.Context, partition int32, offset int64) (bool, error)
	Events(ctx context.Context, orderID string) ([]store.Event, error)
	Apply(ctx context.Context, e store.Event, status store.Status) error
}

type Producer interface {
	Produce(ctx context.Context, records ...kafka.Record) error
}

type Settings struct {
	EventsTopic string
	StatusTopic string
	RetryTopic string
	DeadLetterTopic string
	Attempts int
	MinDelay time.Duration
	MaxDelay time.Duration
}

The Service consumes under queue.AtLeastOnce, so a record is committed only once Process returns nil:

item.title: Retries and dead letters
item.description:
Processing a record

One Process handles both orders.events and orders.retry, and keeps no state of its own:

func (p *Projector) Process(ctx context.Context, m kafka.Message) error {
	attempt, from, err := p.origin(m)
	if err != nil {
		return p.deadLetter(ctx, m, from, reasonMalformed, err, 0)
	}

	e, reason, err := decode(m, from)
	if err != nil {
		return p.deadLetter(ctx, m, from, reason, err, 0)
	}

	err = p.wait(ctx, m, attempt)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	work, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, workDeadline)
	defer cancel()
	reason, err = p.project(work, m, e)
	if err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if ctx.Err() != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("projecting %s, partition %d, offset %d: %w", from.topic, from.partition, from.offset, context.Cause(ctx))
	}
	return p.retry(ctx, m, from, attempt, reason, err)
}
The record Then
malformed, or of an unknown type a dead letter, at once
projected, or applied already committed
unavailable or invalid-transition, below RETRY_ATTEMPTS produced to orders.retry, one attempt higher
the same, at RETRY_ATTEMPTS a dead letter, with its last attempt’s reason
its context ended, at shutdown or a revoke Process returns the error, and the record is processed again
neither orders.retry nor orders.dlq stores it Process returns the error, and the App exits 1 
const (
	reasonMalformed = "malformed"
	reasonUnknownType = "unknown-type"
	reasonInvalidTransition = "invalid-transition"
	reasonUnavailable = "unavailable"
)

The retry headers

A retried record carries its attempt, why it failed, and where it came from on orders.events:

item.title: Init
item.description:
The settings

Everything Init reads, in one struct:

type settings struct {
	Consumer kafka.Settings
	Producer kafka.ProducerSettings
	Projector projector.Settings
	Database *pgxpool.Config
	Probes httphealth.Settings
}

config.Struct sources and checks each one, with what it needs to build the rest. A bad one makes Init fail, and the processor exits 78, naming its variable:

type postgres struct {
	URL *url.URL
	Password string
	CA *x509.CertPool
}

type sourced struct {
	settings
	KafkaCA *x509.CertPool
	KafkaTLS *tls.Config
	Postgres postgres
	TrustedTopics []string
}

func readSettings(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup) (settings, error) {
	env := func(name string) config.Value[string] { return config.Env(s.Process.Environment, name) }
	file := func(name string) config.Value[[]byte] { return env(name).Parse(readFile(s.Host.FS)) }
	list := func(v string) []string { return strings.Split(v, ",") }

	got, err := config.Struct(func(r *config.Resolver) sourced {
		consumer := kafka.DefaultSettings()
		consumer.Brokers = r.Get(env("KAFKA_BROKERS").Map(list).Validate(kafka.CheckBrokers))
		consumer.GroupID = r.Get(env("KAFKA_GROUP_ID").Validate(kafka.CheckGroupID))
		consumer.Delivery = queue.AtLeastOnce
		consumer.SessionTimeout = r.Get(env("KAFKA_SESSION_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(consumer.SessionTimeout).Validate(kafka.CheckSessionTimeout))

		producer := kafka.DefaultProducerSettings()
		producer.DeliveryTimeout = r.Get(env("KAFKA_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(producer.DeliveryTimeout).Validate(kafka.CheckDeliveryTimeout))
		producer.Breaker.OpenFor = r.Get(env("KAFKA_BREAKER_OPEN_FOR").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(producer.Breaker.OpenFor).Validate(kafka.CheckBreakerOpenFor))

		return sourced{
			settings: settings{
				Consumer: consumer,
				Producer: producer,
				Projector: projector.Settings{
					EventsTopic: r.Get(env("KAFKA_EVENTS_TOPIC").Validate(notEmpty)),
					StatusTopic: r.Get(env("KAFKA_STATUS_TOPIC").Validate(notEmpty)),
					RetryTopic: r.Get(env("KAFKA_RETRY_TOPIC").Validate(notEmpty)),
					DeadLetterTopic: r.Get(env("KAFKA_DEAD_LETTER_TOPIC").Validate(notEmpty)),
					Attempts: r.Get(env("RETRY_ATTEMPTS").Parse(strconv.Atoi).Default(defaultRetryAttempts).Validate(positive[int])),
					MinDelay: r.Get(env("RETRY_MIN_DELAY").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(defaultRetryMinDelay).Validate(positive[time.Duration])),
					MaxDelay: r.Get(env("RETRY_MAX_DELAY").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(defaultRetryMaxDelay).Validate(positive[time.Duration])),
				},
				Probes: httphealth.Settings{
					Addr: r.Get(env("PROBES_ADDR").Validate(httphealth.CheckAddr)),
					TLS: r.Get(env("PROBES_TLS_PEM_FILE").Parse(pemTLS(s.Host.FS)).Validate(httphealth.CheckTLS)),
				},
			},
			KafkaCA: r.Get(file("KAFKA_TLS_CA_FILE").Parse(certPool)),
			KafkaTLS: r.Get(env("KAFKA_TLS_CERT_FILE").Parse(pemTLS(s.Host.FS))),
			Postgres: postgres{
				URL: r.Get(env("POSTGRES_URL").Parse(parsePostgresURL).Validate(checkPostgresURL)),
				Password: r.Get(file("POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE").Parse(secret)),
				CA: r.Get(file("POSTGRES_TLS_CA_FILE").Parse(certPool)),
			},
			TrustedTopics: r.Get(env("FAULT_TRUSTED_TOPICS").Parse(topicList).Default(nil)),
		}
	}).Read(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return settings{}, err
	}

const (
	defaultRetryAttempts = 10
	defaultRetryMinDelay = time.Second
	defaultRetryMaxDelay = 5 * time.Minute
)
Variable What it is Default
KAFKA_BROKERS the brokers’ host:ports, separated by commas required
KAFKA_GROUP_ID the consumer group required
KAFKA_EVENTS_TOPIC, KAFKA_STATUS_TOPIC, KAFKA_RETRY_TOPIC, KAFKA_DEAD_LETTER_TOPIC the four topics, each a different one required
KAFKA_TLS_CA_FILE, KAFKA_TLS_CERT_FILE the brokers’ CA, and a file holding the processor’s certificate and key, PEM required
KAFKA_SESSION_TIMEOUT kafka.Settings’ SessionTimeout kafka.DefaultSettings()'
KAFKA_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT, KAFKA_BREAKER_OPEN_FOR kafka.ProducerSettings’ DeliveryTimeout and Breaker.OpenFor kafka.DefaultProducerSettings()'
RETRY_ATTEMPTS attempts before a record is dead-lettered 10
RETRY_MIN_DELAY, RETRY_MAX_DELAY the backoff of a record’s first retry, and the longest 1s and 5m
POSTGRES_URL PostgreSQL’s URL, with its user and database, and no password required
POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE, POSTGRES_TLS_CA_FILE a file holding the password, and PostgreSQL’s CA required
PROBES_ADDR, PROBES_TLS_PEM_FILE the probes’ address, and a file holding their certificate and key, PEM required
FAULT_TRUSTED_TOPICS the topics whose records’ scenarios are trusted, separated by commas none
FAULT_MAX_DELAY the longest delay a scenario injects 10s

The four topics must differ, and the backoff can’t start above its longest:
